explanation: Had been + verb-ing for an action that continued before another past action
example: She had been studying for three hours before dinner.

explanation: Will have been + verb-ing for duration before a future point
example: By June, I will have been teaching for ten years.

rule: Present Perfect vs Past Simple Nuances
explanation: Present perfect for unfinished time periods vs past simple for completed
example: I have visited Paris (in my life) vs I visited Paris last year (specific finished time).

explanation: Was/were going to, would for past plans
example: I was going to call you, but I forgot.

explanation: If + past perfect + would + base verb for past condition affecting present
example: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.

explanation: If + past simple + would have + past participle for present condition affecting past
example: If I were more careful, I would not have made that mistake.

explanation: Had I / Were I / Should I instead of if
example: Had I known earlier, I would have helped.

explanation: Unless, provided that, as long as, on condition that
example: You can borrow my car provided that you return it by 6 PM.

explanation: Wish + past perfect for past regrets; wish + would for annoyance
example: I wish I had listened to your advice.

explanation: Modal + be + past participle or modal + have been + past participle
example: The project must be completed by Friday. / The letter should have been sent yesterday.

explanation: It + passive + that clause / subject + passive + to-infinitive
example: It is believed that the CEO will resign. / The CEO is believed to be resigning.

explanation: Have/get something done for arranging services
example: I had my hair cut. / I got the car repaired.

explanation: Need + verb-ing with passive meaning
example: The house needs cleaning. (= needs to be cleaned)

explanation: Tense backshift in reported statements; optional with universal truths
example: She said she was tired ("I am tired"). / He said the Earth revolves around the Sun (no backshift for facts).

explanation: Verb + that clause / verb + to-infinitive / verb + object + to-infinitive
example: He admitted stealing the money. / She advised me to see a doctor.

explanation: Wh-word or if/whether + statement word order, no question mark
example: She asked where I lived. / He asked if I had finished.

explanation: Tell/ask/order + object + to-infinitive
example: The teacher told us to be quiet. / She asked me to open the window.

explanation: Non-defining adds extra info with commas; defining is essential
example: My sister, who lives in London, is a doctor. (non-defining) vs The woman who lives next door is a doctor. (defining)

rule: Whose, Where, When, Why, Preposition + Which
explanation: Relative adverbs and prepositional relatives
example: The house where I grew up. / The reason why I left. / The person to whom I spoke.

explanation: All/most/some/none + of + whom/which in formal English
example: The students, most of whom had passed, celebrated.

explanation: Replacing relative clause with -ing, -ed, or to-infinitive
example: The girl sitting there is my sister. (= who is sitting)

explanation: Must/might/may/could/can't + have + past participle
example: He must have left early. / She can't have seen us.

explanation: Must, have to, should, ought to, need to, needn't, don't have to, mustn't
example: You must wear a seatbelt. / You needn't have come early.

explanation: Would rather + base verb (preference); had better + base verb (strong advice)
example: I would rather stay home. / You had better see a doctor.

explanation: Dare/need + base verb (usually negative or interrogative)
example: I dare not tell him. / Need I say more?

explanation: Never, rarely, seldom, hardly, scarcely, no sooner, not only, not until, nowhere
example: Never have I seen such beauty. / Not only did he finish first, but he also broke the record.

explanation: Should, were, had at start of conditional sentences
example: Were I you, I would apologize. / Should you need help, call me.

explanation: So + adjective + auxiliary + subject; such + be + noun
example: So beautiful was the sunset that everyone stopped to watch.

explanation: Suggest, recommend, insist, demand, propose + that + base verb
example: I suggest that he see a doctor. / They insisted that she be present.

rule: It's Time / Would Rather + Past Subjunctive
explanation: It's time + past subjunctive; would rather + past subjunctive
example: It's time we left. / I would rather you didn't smoke.

rule: As If/As Though + Past/ Past Perfect
explanation: Unreal comparison using past or past perfect
example: He acts as if he owned the place. / She looked as though she had seen a ghost.

explanation: To, in order to, so as to, so that, in case, for + noun/gerund
example: I left early so that I wouldn't miss the train. / Take an umbrella in case it rains.

explanation: So + adjective + that; such + noun + that
example: The movie was so boring that I fell asleep. / It was such a hot day that we stayed inside.

explanation: Although, even though, despite, in spite of, while, whereas
example: Despite being tired, she continued working. / While I agree with you, I cannot support your plan.

explanation: -ing, -ed, and having + past participle clauses for adverbial meaning
example: Having finished his homework, he went out to play. / Exhausted by the journey, she went straight to bed.

explanation: It + be + emphasized element + that/who; What-clause + be
example: It was John who broke the window. / What I need is a relaxing holiday.

explanation: Moving an element to the front of the sentence
example: A very strange experience it was. / Into the room walked the principal.

explanation: Omitting repeated words; using do/so/not to replace
example: She can speak French, and he can too. / "Will it rain?" "I think so." / "Is she coming?" "I hope not."

explanation: Sort of, kind of, apparently, presumably, roughly, about, around
example: It is arguably the most important invention. / There were about fifty people.

explanation: Furthermore, moreover, nevertheless, consequently, accordingly, in contrast
example: The experiment failed. Consequently, we must revise our hypothesis.

explanation: This/that/these/those referring back; one/ones substitution
example: The new policy has flaws. This is why we oppose it. / I need a pen. I don't have one.

explanation: Synonyms, antonyms, hyponyms, collocations for text cohesion
example: The car broke down. The vehicle was towed away. (lexical chain)

explanation: Present tense used when discussing literature, even for past events in a story
example: In the novel, Hamlet struggles with his conscience and ultimately decides to avenge his father.

explanation: Questions asked for effect, not requiring an answer
example: Who can deny the importance of education? / Is that really the best you can do?

explanation: Using the same grammatical structure for balance and rhythm
example: She came, she saw, she conquered. / It is better to be late than to be unprepared.
